export_controls.text: Productive meeting this morning with NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang. As AI policy reaches a pivotal moment, NVIDIA’s expanding U.S. investments shows  what’s possible when we prioritize innovation at home. china_race_dynamics.text:
I’ve been seeing a lot of conversation around the AI race with China, and I absolutely want the United States to lead. But we can’t forget about protecting our kids in the process.

Big Tech is controlling children. If that doesn’t change, the future we’re building won’t be worth it.

https://t.co/78uxObBxLy

deepseek.reason: The speaker says he absolutely wants the United States to lead in the AI race with China.

china_race_dynamics.text:
Getting a briefing from @sama on AI. 

Everyone agrees AI is going to be disruptive to the economy, in both good and bad ways. 

Question is, how can we build guardrails for the US to capitalize on these innovations (vs. say the CCP) while protecting American workers? https://t.co/2zeQyMaR3V

deepseek.confidence_reason: The CCP comparison and innovation framing imply competition priority, though the statement is phrased as a question about guardrails.
